strengths: Addresses an important and practically relevant problem: improving safety, feasibility, and rule compliance in learned autonomous-driving planners trained from imperfect human demonstrations.

Empirical results on nuPlan are promising, especially in reactive closed-loop simulation without post-processing, where Plan-R1 improves over strong learning-based baselines across the reported splits.
The paper includes useful ablations for the fine-tuning stage, KL regularization, and pass@k behavior, plus qualitative cases showing correction of speeding, off-road driving, and collision failures.
weaknesses: Novelty is moderate. The core ingredients--motion-token autoregressive planning, rule-based planning rewards, benchmark-metric-style rewards, and RL fine-tuning--are all close to prior work; the LLM/GRPO analogy feels more like repackaging than a major conceptual advance.

Important implementation details are missing despite being referenced as appendix material: reward components and weights, token vocabulary settings, model size, GRPO group size, sampling details, hyperparameters, training compute, and post-processing configuration. The SOTA claim is overstated. In Table 1, Plan-R1 is not best on several non-reactive settings, and Plan-R1* is below Diffusion Planner* on Test14-hard reactive; the strongest evidence is narrower, mainly reactive closed-loop performance without post-processing.

The RL formulation raises technical concerns: the frozen learned world model is used for fine-tuning but evaluation uses nuPlan/IDM dynamics, with little validation that the learned reactive model is accurate under counterfactual ego actions. This may introduce exploitable model bias or distribution shift.

The evaluation lacks key controls: no comparison to PPO or simpler reward-weighted/rejection-sampling fine-tuning, no reward-term ablations, no isolation of the refinement post-processor’s contribution, and no variance or statistical significance for stochastic sampling results.
The pass@k analysis is hard to interpret for actual planning unless the system has a non-oracle mechanism to select the successful trajectory among k samples.

Because the reward appears closely aligned with nuPlan scoring metrics, the results may reflect benchmark-specific optimization; broader generalization evidence across datasets, scenario distributions, or safety-critical edge cases is missing.
